title: The Demise of Democracy Isn’t Here Yet | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Michael Froman argues reports of democracy's demise are premature, citing record or near-record turnout in recent Serbian, Brazilian, and Israeli elections, with youth participation as the common thread. Serbia's student movement ousted Vučić, Lula won a fourth term on a digital mobilization surge, and Israel's high-turnout vote produced a hung Knesset, leaving governance questions open.

insights.claim: Despite alarming data on press freedom, illiberal turns, and election integrity concerns, recent elections show notable positive signs for democracy worldwide.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Political-risk narratives of uniform democratic decline may be overstated; regime change via ballot remains possible.
insights.locator: The fate of democracy around the world

insights.claim: High voter participation, and possibly youth turnout, is the throughline across recent elections in Serbia, Brazil, and Israel, even though their outcomes diverged ideologically.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Turnout surges, especially youth-driven, can be a leading indicator of incumbent vulnerability.
insights.quote: If there is a throughline, it is the level of participation—and perhaps the role of the youth.

insights.claim: Reports of democracy's demise may be premature, and young voters may deserve credit for that.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Youth-mobilized anti-corruption movements are a recurring political-change pattern to monitor in emerging markets.
insights.locator: For now, though, reports of democracy

insights.claim: Serbia's October 25, 2026 election had turnout near 70 percent, its highest since Yugoslavia's breakup in 1992.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Mass participation signals a strong mandate for the new government.
insights.locator: Serbia held an election that saw voter turnout

insights.claim: In Serbia, the opposition Student List won 53 percent of the vote and 141 of 250 parliamentary seats, while Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party got under 40 percent, and Vučić conceded.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: A clear majority for the opposition implies a material policy shift in Serbia after more than a decade of Vučić rule.
insights.locator: During the elections held last Sunday

insights.claim: Serbia's student protest movement formed less than two years before the election after a railway station disaster killed sixteen people, and grew into a broad anti-government movement as evidence pointed to government fraud and corruption.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Corruption-linked infrastructure failures can catalyze rapid political upheaval.
insights.locator: The movement was formed less than two years ago

insights.claim: Serbia's new student-led majority must convert political momentum into good policies and governance, and what comes next in Belgrade is hard to read.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Governance uncertainty for an inexperienced ruling movement creates near-term policy risk in Serbia.
insights.quote: It needs to focus on turning that momentum into good policies and good governance.

insights.claim: Hungary's April 2026 election saw strong youth turnout help Péter Magyar's Tisza Party end Viktor Orbán's sixteen-year reign on an anti-corruption campaign, a pattern repeated in Serbia.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Successive defeats of entrenched Central European populists suggest a regional political shift with EU-relations implications.
insights.locator: Like his friend up the Danube

themes.theme: Brazil: Lula's comeback via digital mobilization

insights.claim: Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff with 51.8 percent to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2 percent, a margin of 4.4 million votes, securing a fourth term at age eighty-one.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Continuity of left-leaning government in Brazil for another term shapes fiscal and policy expectations.
insights.locator: In Brazil, Lula surged to a comeback victory

insights.claim: A WhatsApp channel called Lula's Army, launched by a forty-two-year-old congressman, grew to ten million members and drove Lula's mobilization despite restrictions on sharing some of his social media posts.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Messaging platforms are now decisive electoral infrastructure, raising regulatory and political stakes for platforms like WhatsApp.
insights.locator: Lula was propelled to victory in no small part

insights.claim: In Brazil's first round more than thirty-three million people (21 percent of voters) did not vote; in the runoff blank and null votes hit their lowest level of the century and 3 million first-round abstainers turned out, mostly for Lula.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Turnout swings among disengaged voters can flip close elections, complicating poll-based forecasting.
insights.locator: The effect of this massive mobilization

insights.claim: Lula became the first candidate since 1989 to win Brazil's presidency after finishing runner-up in the first round.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: First-round results are an unreliable predictor of runoff outcomes in Brazil.
insights.locator: The effect of this massive mobilization

insights.claim: Israel's election turnout reached 77.7 percent, its highest since 1999, with an estimated sixty-seven thousand Israelis abroad flying home to vote in what was seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's nineteen years in power.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: High engagement signals a contested mandate on Netanyahu's handling of Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran.
insights.locator: In Israel, election turnout hit 77.7 percent

insights.claim: No bloc won a Knesset majority: Netanyahu's bloc took fifty-three seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc forty-eight, and Arab parties a historic nineteen, leaving Israeli governance murky.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Prolonged coalition uncertainty in Israel raises policy and regional security risk premium.
insights.quote: the future of Israeli governance is murky at best
insights.locator: In Israel, election turnout hit 77.7 percent

insights.claim: Roughly 640,000 Israelis aged eighteen to twenty-two, about 10 percent of the electorate, were eligible to vote.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Young voters form a meaningful swing bloc in Israeli politics.

themes.theme: From protest to governance and upcoming elections

insights.claim: A healthy election does not guarantee a government able to overcome polarization and gridlock, and turning protest into lasting change is difficult.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Electoral upsets do not automatically translate into reform; policy delivery risk persists.
insights.quote: a healthy election does not guarantee a government that can overcome polarization and gridlock

insights.claim: Maria Ressa cited journalism and protests in the Philippines, which led to Rodrigo Duterte being sent to the ICC in The Hague, and daily protests in Georgia and Serbia as signs democracy remains alive.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Accountability mechanisms for former leaders can reshape political risk in affected countries.

insights.claim: Upcoming major elections include Spain next month, a consequential French presidential election in spring, and highly uncertain U.S. midterms.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: A dense election calendar into 2027 is a source of European and U.S. political-risk volatility.
insights.locator: Next month, we’ll see major elections
